description: The whitened base point of the linear ring at sigma^2 = 0, and the path of every sweep: N = 512, hidden length_scale 2, P = 256, m = n = 4, K = 3, beta 10 (target condensation, tau = 0.77, 0.21, 0.15), B = 32, spatial.parametrisation whitened, lr 0.96, 10^4 epochs, records every 25 epochs. linear_teacher with an orthonormal teacher and latents uniform on [0, 1]; L = 1, phi id, g 1; k0 = k1 = 1 (input and output kernels of length_scale 0 and amplitude 1, weight_lambda 1); r = rate_lambda = 0; SGLD, float64; every population on the deterministic grid with box = N, so length scales are in sites; init prior. One sample per member, its final state; statistics are read off the member-averaged final-state spectrum with bootstrap errors over members, after removing the frequencies the penalty floor raises (min_rel_eig of the top hidden eigenvalue) from both paths' spectra; the records feed only the relaxation diagnostic. Regime (exact posterior from a Gibbs sampler run off-repo, 512 chains, against predicted_spectra, modes 1/2/3): R(1)/R(0) 0.9343/0.8916/0.8890 against 0.9350/0.8924/0.8896, R(2)/R(0) 0.7736/0.6352/0.6268 against 0.7757/0.6378/0.6289, band share (|q| <= 24) 0.664/0.483/0.474 against 0.668/0.486/0.476, Gaussian width at 2 sites 2.79/2.10/2.07 against 2.81/2.11/2.08, mode-1/mode-2 band power ratio 25.7 against 25.6: within 0.1 to 0.8 SE at B_max = 128 (B = 32 and its fourfold extension), the accuracy budget of one SE at B_max. predicted_spectra is the N -> infinity limit and leaves out the readout's (n/2) log det term, an O(n/N) correction; at N = 256 these errors would reach 1.1 SE at B_max. The data term moves the same statistics from the prior by 33/5/3.5 SE at B = 32 (R(1)/R(0)), 31/4.7/3.3 (R(2)/R(0)), 21/3.1/2.2 (band share) and 12 (ratio); the budget is fct.linear_ring.budget_se. Rule (fct.linear_ring.disagrees): an agreement test fails when |observed - predicted| exceeds FALSIFY_N_SE = 3 bootstrap SEs at the run's B, and a failure counts only if it persists after `exp extend` to FOLLOW_UP_FACTOR = 4 times B. The lr is 0.9 of what the run-start check accepts: lr lambda_max(loss Hessian) = 0.885 at the prior initial state (lambda_max 0.922; refused at 1). At stationarity lambda_max is 1.19, so lr lambda_max = 1.14, past the check's own bound (it is checked only at the start), and the stiffest mode's variance is inflated about 2.3x. Measured against lr 0.2 (B = 32, both stationary), lr 0.96 shifts R(1)/R(0) and R(2)/R(0) of mode 1 by -1.2 to -1.3 SE at B_max = 128, mode 1's band share by -0.7 SE and the ratio by -1.3 SE (modes 2 and 3 by at most 0.25 SE). That bias alone exceeds the one-SE accuracy budget, so by the plan's rule the regime is not accurate at this lr: a disagreement in mode 1's statistics or the ratio at this lr is not evidence against the theory. Relaxation from the prior, measured at lr 0.96 and 0.2 with B = 256: mode 1's low-q power rises in a fast phase (time constant 6-7 lr-epoch units, about 75% of the rise) and a slow tail (17-20 units), the same in lr units at both lrs; the statistics' deficit falls below 0.2 SE at B_max by lr t = 85, about 90 epochs here, so 10^4 epochs leave none. In one run of this preset (B = 32, GPU, 108 s) the relaxation fit (fct.linear_ring.relaxation_fit) of the second half of the records left a deficit of 0 with an SE of 0.0001 to 0.0009 on every statistic (0.09 on the ratio), under 0.1 of the budget. Its final-state statistics lay 1.5 to 2.3 SE at B_max below the prediction on every mode (band share of mode 2 +0.2). On modes 2 and 3 about -0.5 to -1.0 SE of that is a real offset, present at lr 0.2 too (the theory's finite-N error, inside the regime budget), and the rest is one draw of 32 members (its SE is twice the SE at B_max, and the statistics share the members, so they move together); `exp extend` to B = 128 is the check. On mode 1 the lr bias adds to it. This preset and `linear_ring_equivalence` have the same exp hash and setting directory (the exp hash covers only the axes), so they must be run in separate ROOTs. Run plan: this setting and its penalty twin (`linear_ring_equivalence`) at the base point first, then the beta and k sweeps on this whitened path only (`--axis 'train.beta=[...]'` with a matching lr, each at 0.9 of its own check, and a new regime check per point). Cost: about 10 ms per epoch for all 32 members on an RTX 4500 Ada GPU in float64 (29 ms on 8 CPU threads), under two minutes of GPU time.
